issues.claim: Full audit body (title through the 'Prepared from publicly available information' line)
issues.problem: Body runs roughly 530 words, about 80 over the ~450 ceiling in the brief.
issues.fix: Cut ~80 words: shorten the three 'What the agent would do' paragraphs, drop the third 'Why this works' bullet or fold it into the second, and tighten the opener paragraph.

issues.claim: "roughly $12,000-$35,000 a year of lookup and research time" (Section 3)
issues.problem: Not derivable from the assumptions behind it. The underlying model is 15-25% recovery across 0.75-1.5 FTE at the NJ median CSR wage of $47,740 loaded 1.2-1.3x, which computes to about $6,400-$23,300. $35,000 is only reachable using the NJ 90th percentile ($72,040), which is not the stated basis. The range is inflated relative to its own assumption.
issues.fix: Restate as 'roughly $6,000-$23,000 a year of lookup and research time' (or raise the recovery assumption to 25-45% and say so in the body). Also add the one-line basis (FTE share x NJ median x loading) so the number is auditable.

issues.claim: "you publish every carrier's claims number as a standing reference" (Section 3)
issues.problem: Contradicted on the cited page: the Mutual of Omaha entry lists claims and service as 'See website' rather than a number. 39 of 40 entries carry numbers.
issues.fix: Change 'every' to 'nearly every' or 'each carrier's claims and service contacts, mostly direct numbers'.

issues.claim: "every way a customer can start something runs through a phone call or a web form" (opening paragraph, echoed in the email as "quote requests come in by form or phone only")
issues.problem: The site also publishes a general office email address in the header bar, and the offices are walk-in locations, so 'every way / only' overstates a two-channel picture. Not supported as written.
issues.fix: Say 'quote requests arrive by phone, web form or email' and keep the substantive point (no booking, no instant quote, no chat).

issues.claim: "someone sorts out by hand which of the three brands owns each lead"
issues.problem: Presented as fact but this is an inference about internal routing; nothing public shows how leads are assigned. Same issue in Section 2 with 'businesses like yours usually have someone opening...' (that one is at least hedged with 'usually').
issues.fix: Attribute it: 'as far as we can tell from the outside, someone has to decide which of the three brands owns each lead' - or move it into a clearly labelled inference sentence.

issues.claim: Section heading "Every quote request gets an answer the same hour"
issues.problem: Overpromises relative to the stated human-approval gate: the agent acknowledges instantly but a producer approves anything client-facing, so a substantive 'answer' in the same hour is not what the design delivers.
issues.fix: Retitle to 'Every quote request gets acknowledged within the hour - even Sunday night'.

issues.claim: "It plugs into what you already run: the existing quote forms, the Bridge upload portal, your calendar and shared inbox."
issues.problem: The quote forms and the crm.bridge.insure upload link are verified; the agency's calendar and shared inbox are assumptions, not documented anywhere, and are stated as existing systems.
issues.fix: Hedge: 'the existing quote forms and secure upload portal, plus the calendar and inbox your team already uses'.

issues.claim: "You run three agency brands - Edison, Belford and Tinton Falls"
issues.problem: Minor: the brands are Fraser Brothers, DeLaurier and Kennedy & Ward; the towns are the locations, not the brand names. Also 'where mistakes cost the most' (Section 3) and 'Coverage answers are also where mistakes cost the most' is an unsupported E&O assertion presented as fact.
issues.fix: Write 'three agency brands across Edison, Belford and Tinton Falls' and soften the E&O line to 'where mistakes tend to be most expensive'.
